To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in selected patients with CIA and IIA lesions, unilateral stenting of the contralaterally stenosed artery is sufficient to improve both limbs, and the long-term patency rate is 100%.
in selected patients with chronic occlusion in one iliac artery and stenosis of the other, unilateral angioplasty of the stenotic iliac artery alone improves blood flow in both limbs.

in selected patients with CIA and/or IIA stenotic lesions and long-term occlusion of the contra-lateral iliac artery, unilateral dilation/stent-ing of the stenotic lesion alone increases blood flow, improves symptoms, and maintains patency of the stented artery during a 24-month period.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of the stenting of the common and/or internal iliac artery, on the blood flow of the limbs, in patients with a chronic iliac occlusion.
the development of a new class of materials, namely, poly(ester urea)s (PEU), which can be used for the preparation of polyurethanes with improved properties for medical applications.
the development of a new method for the treatment of chronic occlusion of both the common and internal iliac arteries, which has the potential to improve blood flow to both the legs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
unilateral iliac artery stenting improves both limbs in patients with bilateral iliac artery disease.

unilateral dilation/stenting in selected patients with CIA and/or IIA stenotic lesions in the presence of contralateral chronic occlusion of both the CIA/EIA and IIA can improve blood flow and symptoms to both limbs.
unilateral iliac stenting in the setting of bilateral iliac disease is safe and efficacious, and that the results are sustained over a 2-year follow-up period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
unilateral stent placement in the iliac axis is sufficient in selected patients with chronic occlusions of the contralateralside iliac artery.
in patients with chronic occlusion and contralateral stenosis, stenting the stenosis is enough.
the results of this study support the concept that the hemodynamic and clinical benefit of angioplasty/stent treatment of a stenosis in the iliac artery can extend to the chronically occluded side.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in selected patients with bilateral iliac lesions, unilateral iliac artery stenting can be a safe and effective treatment for both limbs.
in selected patients with chronic occlusion and a stenosis on the other side, unilateral treatment of the stenotic side is sufficient and can improve symptoms in both limbs.

in selected patients with chronic iliac occlusion and contralateral iliofemoral stenosis, unilateral stenting of the iliofem-femoral axis can improve the blood flow to the occluded side and alleviate the symptoms in both limbs, without the need for contralateral intervention.
